finding.claim: GET /users returns the id and name of every user in any org the caller names. Nothing checks that the caller is authenticated or belongs to that org, so this is an IDOR / broken access control. Severity depends on whether auth middleware exists outside this file; none is visible in the only source file.
finding.source: req.query.org, an unauthenticated, attacker-chosen query parameter
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") with the result returned via res.json(rows)

trace.note: Express app is created with no auth, session or tenant middleware registered (app.use is never called)
Route handler registered with no per-route authorization
req.query.org is used directly as the tenant filter, so the caller picks which org's data to read
Matching rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: SQL injection is not possible, because the query is parameterized ($1). I looked for authentication or authorization middleware, a session-derived org, or a role check and found none in this file. req.pg is injected by code outside this repo, so a tenant-scoped connection there (for example Postgres row-level security) could mitigate this and could not be verified. The other routes were checked and are not vulnerable. /file resolves the path under ROOT and enforces a ROOT+sep prefix check, and sendFile also rejects dotfiles. /count runs execFile with fixed arguments and no user input.

verdict.guard_found: none (parameterized query only prevents SQLi; no auth, session or tenant check; req.pg is set outside this repo and no other source file exists)
verdict.reason: db.js:5-10 registers no middleware, and db.js:9 uses the anonymous req.query.org as the org filter and db.js:10 returns the rows, so any caller can read any org's users; the only unverifiable mitigation is a tenant-scoped req.pg, which nothing in the repo suggests.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (query is parameterized, which only prevents SQL injection; no authn/authz check or session-derived org in the handler)
verdict_facts.reason: db.js:9 passes the client-supplied req.query.org straight into the users query and db.js:10 returns the rows, with no check against req.user or any role. The upstream middleware only populates identity, so nothing in the code restricts which org the caller can read.
